description: FNET/GridEye is a wide-area frequency measurement network operated by the Power Information Technology Laboratory at the University of Tennessee. The public site, read on 2026-09-26, describes low-cost GPS-synchronised Frequency Disturbance Recorders plugged into ordinary 120 V outlets that measure frequency, phase angle and voltage and stream them over the internet to servers at the University of Tennessee and Virginia Tech. Public displays include a table display, a frequency gauge, an angle contour map, a US frequency gradient map, a world-wide frequency map, spectrum, time error and sample events. The laboratory uses the data for event detection and location, oscillation detection, renewable integration studies, islanding detection, control inputs and instability prediction. Members of the FNET/GridEye Industry Consortium receive automatic event alert e-mails with event size in MW and location and have access to an event website; data beyond the public displays are obtained by contacting the laboratory. No licence is stated. Caveats: public views are displays, not downloads. Simulation uses are validating dynamic models against measured frequency events, generator trip and oscillation studies, and inertia monitoring.
